reviewKind: independent correction re-review of three deadline findings
settingsEvidence: Retained explicitly user-confirmed inherited batch; no model override.
scope: Correction of RM402-INLINE-READ-DEADLINE, RM402-BACKOFF-DEADLINE-MAPPING and RM402-TIMEOUT-CONTROL-STATEMENT-CLASSIFICATION, including transaction-local server timeout and acknowledged/unknown commit boundaries. No source fixes or broad concurrent builds.

corrections.reason: Policy-free nonmutative inline actions now receive rootPersistence.withDeadline(__operation.deadlineAt).withSignal(__operation.signal).withOperationTime(__operation.now). Direct queries use the bounded client, and the helper checks expiry before another operation and after the active query returns.
corrections.regressionEvidence: The inline fixture has two direct required reads. PostgreSQL uses an exclusive table lock released after the 200ms route budget; SQLite delays Statement.all for 300ms and asserts reads=1 plus 504. The corrected all interception matches policyReadRows lowering. Main reports the PostgreSQL case passed; the reviewer inspected the source and test but did not independently execute the compiled inline HTTP route.
corrections.limit: The inline PostgreSQL read is outside a transaction, so this proves cooperative expiry after read settlement, not server interruption of that read.

corrections.reason: A terminal fault with known no_commit evidence receives RequestDeadlineFault when the explicit route deadline has expired. Existing transaction evidence and constraint identity are preserved. Unknown faults are excluded, and retry-window-only exhaustion without an explicit expired route deadline retains its original mapping.
corrections.independentEvidence: An in-memory source-extracted retry loop with deadline t=20 and wait settlement t=21 produced one attempt, deadlineExceeded=true, and the identical no_commit evidence object. Separate probes preserved an acknowledged result after expiry, the identical unknown commit fault, and the original fault without a deadline marker on retry-window-only exhaustion.
corrections.regressionEvidence: The checked-in runtime test uses a structured first-attempt SQLITE_BUSY or PostgreSQL trigger SQLSTATE 40001, advances the monotonic clock during backoff, and asserts 504, one attempt and no stored row.

corrections.reason: Timeout setup/refresh/reset and PostgreSQL savepoint controls now pass through the classified helper. callbackState changes to failed before setup, and the failed-callback branch recognizes structured 57014 only with elapsed attempt-deadline evidence. Cleanup release/rollback intentionally bypass cancellation/deadline prechecks; their typed failures can still be classified at the outer callback boundary. COMMIT remains outside this deadline conversion branch.
corrections.independentEvidence: Source-extracted production fault types, classification/helper functions, client wrappers and transaction method passed eight cases: setup, refresh, reset and savepoint, each with expiry true and false. All produced PersistenceFault and no_commit evidence; the deadline marker was present exactly in expired cases.
corrections.regressionEvidence: The checked-in test exposes createPersistenceClient only in its disposable generated test module, injects errno=57014 for the four control phases, and asserts typed failure, expiry-sensitive deadline marker and no-commit transaction evidence. No production test export is emitted.

independentProbe.command: bun --no-install --env-file=/dev/null run - (in-memory source-extracted TypeScript, Bun.Transpiler, deterministic clock/jitter and fake PostgreSQL controls)
independentProbe.limits: Synthetic probes verify emitted branch logic, not network/server behavior or a full compiled application. The first extraction omitted multiline function headers and failed to parse; it supplied no correctness evidence. The corrected extraction included complete emitted functions and all stated probes passed. No files or build outputs were created by the probes.

serverBoundAndCommitLimits: Transaction-local PostgreSQL statement_timeout is set from the remaining monotonic budget and refreshed before client statements. This is a server statement bound; network delay, connection acquisition and BEGIN are not thereby bounded.

Nontransactional PostgreSQL queries, including the inline-read regression, retain cooperative checks. SQLite calls remain synchronous. Abort without deadline expiry remains cooperative. Do not claim a hard whole-request response bound.

The callback checks the budget before resetting statement_timeout, resets it before COMMIT, then checks again. Once COMMIT starts, acknowledged success remains authoritative even if cancellation/deadline arrives; a lost acknowledgment stays unknown and is never blindly replayed. A long COMMIT may outlive the route budget.

Authority-log insertion and cleanup use their existing adapter paths; a previous timeout setting is not proof of a freshly computed hard bound for every control or log statement. These limits do not reopen the corrected cooperative mapping findings.
